proposals.before: The emperor saw that he was steady and substantial, fluent in argument, versed in legal precedent, and could dress Legalist practice in Confucian language; he delighted in him, and within a year Hong rose to Left Metropolitan Superintendent.
proposals.after: The emperor saw that he was steady and substantial, fluent in argument, versed in the affairs of law clerks, and trimmed these with Confucian learning; he delighted in him, and within a year Hong rose to Left Metropolitan Superintendent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 緣飾以儒術 ornaments clerk-law practice with Confucian learning; idiomatic invents an explicit Legalist school label not in the source.

proposals.before: The execution of Zhufu Yan and Dong Zhongshu's banishment to Jiaoxi were Hong's work.
proposals.after: The killing of Zhufu Yan and Dong Zhongshu's transfer to Jiaoxi were Hong's work.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徙 means transfer/relocation; idiomatic 'banishment' overstates the source wording.

proposals.before: Hong's son Du inherited the marquisate; having been governor of Shanyang for more than ten years, an edict summoned Magistrate Shi Cheng of Juye to the Public Carriage office; Du detained him and did not dispatch him; sitting judgment he was sentenced to wall labor.
proposals.after: Hong's son Du inherited the marquisate; having been governor of Shanyang for more than ten years, an edict summoned Shi Cheng, magistrate of Juye, to the Public Carriage office; Du detained him and did not dispatch him; for this offense he was sentenced to wall labor.
proposals.reason: Literal 'sitting judgment' calques 坐論 awkwardly; clarify that Du was the one sentenced for detaining the magistrate.

proposals.before: At Luoyang he learned Er Kuan had the seal—and laughed aloud.
proposals.after: At Luoyang he learned Er Kuan held the post—and laughed aloud.
proposals.reason: Chinese 為之 means held the vacant office, not possession of a seal; 'had the seal' invents an image absent from the source.

proposals.before: The sovereign meant to wield both wen and wu and hunted talent as if starved for it—he fetched Mei Sheng with the herb-wheeled cart and caught his breath at the sight of Zhufu Yan.
proposals.after: The sovereign meant to wield both wen and wu and hunted talent as if starved for it—he fetched Mei Sheng with the rush-wheeled cart and caught his breath at the sight of Zhufu Yan.
proposals.reason: 蒲輪 is the rush/cattail-padded wheeled carriage for honored guests, not an 'herb-wheeled' cart; literal already has rush-wheeled.

proposals.before: Never did the dynasty gather talent so thickly: Hong, Dong, and Kuan for classical breadth; the Shi brothers for steadfast service; Ji An and Bu Shi for blunt loyalty; Han Anguo and Zheng Dangshi for lifting others; Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang for codifying law; Sima Qian and Xiangru for voice; jesters Dongfang Shuo and Mei Gao; debaters Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen; calendar-makers Tang Dou and Luoxia Hong; the harmonist Li Yan'nian; the reckoner Sang Hongyang; envoys Zhang Qian and Su Wu; blades Wei Qing and Huo Qubing; regents Huo Guang and Jin Midi—and a cloud of names besides.
proposals.after: Never did the dynasty gather talent so thickly: Hong, Dong, and Kuan for classical breadth; the Shi brothers for steadfast service; Ji An and Bu Shi for blunt loyalty; Han Anguo and Zheng Dangshi for lifting others; Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang for codifying law; Sima Qian and Xiangru for voice; jesters Dongfang Shuo and Mei Gao; debaters Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen; calendar-makers Tang Du and Luoxia Hong; the harmonist Li Yan'nian; the reckoner Sang Hongyang; envoys Zhang Qian and Su Wu; blades Wei Qing and Huo Qubing; regents Huo Guang and Jin Midi—and a cloud of names besides.
proposals.reason: 唐都 is Tang Du (都 dú/dū), not Tang Dou; Dou misreads the given name.

proposals.before: Thus Han obtained men; at this time it was most flourishing: in Confucian elegance then Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, Er Kuan; in steadfast conduct then Shi Jian, Shi Qing; in plain straightforwardness then Ji An, Bu Shi; in advancing the worthy then Han Anguo, Zheng Dangshi; in fixing statutes then Zhao Yu, Zhang Tang; in literary composition then Sima Qian, Xiangru; in jest then Dongfang Shuo, Mei Gao; in repartee then Yan Zhu, Zhu Maichen; in calendrical reckoning then Tang Dou, Luoxia Hong; in harmonizing pitch then Li Yan'nian; in planning transport then Sang Hongyang; as envoys then Zhang Qian, Su Wu; as generals then Wei Qing, Huo Qubing; as testamentary appointees then Huo Guang, Jin Midi—the rest cannot be fully recorded.
proposals.after: Thus Han obtained men; at this time it was most flourishing: in Confucian elegance then Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, Er Kuan; in steadfast conduct then Shi Jian, Shi Qing; in plain straightforwardness then Ji An, Bu Shi; in advancing the worthy then Han Anguo, Zheng Dangshi; in fixing statutes then Zhao Yu, Zhang Tang; in literary composition then Sima Qian, Xiangru; in jest then Dongfang Shuo, Mei Gao; in repartee then Yan Zhu, Zhu Maichen; in calendrical reckoning then Tang Du, Luoxia Hong; in harmonizing pitch then Li Yan'nian; in planning transport then Sang Hongyang; as envoys then Zhang Qian, Su Wu; as generals then Wei Qing, Huo Qubing; as testamentary appointees then Huo Guang, Jin Midi—the rest cannot be fully recorded.
proposals.reason: 唐都 is Tang Du, not Tang Dou; same given-name misreading as in the idiomatic line.

decisions.reason: s0084 has 習文法吏事，緣飾以儒術: practiced in clerk-law affairs and ornamented with Confucian learning. “Legalist practice” invents a school label absent from the Chinese; the proposed wording restores that sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 習文法吏事，緣飾以儒術

decisions.reason: s0119 reads 殺主父偃，徙董仲舒膠西: kill Zhufu Yan and transfer Dong Zhongshu to Jiaoxi. 徙 is relocation/transfer; “banishment” overstates the source verb.

In 度留不遣，坐論為城旦, 坐論 marks Du as convicted and sentenced for detaining the magistrate. “Sitting judgment” calques awkwardly and can be misread as Du judging someone else; the proposed gloss clarifies the agent.
Context s0248 concerns the vacant 御史大夫; s0249’s 聞兒寬為之 means Er Kuan held that post. “Had the seal” invents seal imagery not in 為之.
蒲輪 is the rush/cattail-padded wheeled carriage for honored guests, not an herb-wheeled cart; “herb-wheeled” misreads 蒲.
歷數則唐都 names Tang Du (都 dú/dū); “Tang Dou” misreads the given name 都.
The same 唐都 in s0258 is Tang Du, not Tang Dou; the literal field needs the same given-name correction as the idiomatic line.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0006 shows “Tang Dou” exists only as the bad English spelling of 唐都; s0258 supports Tang Du (already claimed in c0252), leaving no source support for this Dou form.
